name: FrontierMath: Open Problems
description: A collection of unsolved mathematical research problems designed to test whether AI systems can advance the frontier of human mathematical knowledge. Problems are drawn from open research questions where professional mathematicians have tried and failed to solve them, with the constraint that proposed solutions must be programmatically verifiable. At release the set contained 14 open problems spanning number theory, combinatorics, algebraic geometry, and topology, ranging from 'moderately interesting' to 'breakthrough' level — none known to be solved by humans or AI at that time.
evaluation_method: programmatic verification of proposed solutions; scored as solved / unsolved per problem
general_score_metric: count and identity of problems solved (each solution is a stand-alone result, not aggregated into a single accuracy)
typical_sota_score: March 2026: GPT-5.4 Pro produced the first AI solution to a previously open FrontierMath problem (Epoch AI verified); broad accuracy aggregates not meaningful at this scale
reputation: Successor track to FrontierMath (Tiers 1–4); developed and owned independently by Epoch AI (the original FrontierMath was OpenAI-funded); cited as the canonical example of benchmarking targeted well above human-expert ability.
notes: Distinct from the main FrontierMath benchmark (Tiers 1–4): Open Problems contains genuinely unsolved problems rather than expert-crafted ones with private known answers. Each task is more like a case study than a benchmark item; solving even one is a research-grade event. As of release, OpenAI was the only entity to have purchased verifier access. Only graded outputs that can be programmatically verified are admitted.
